notes:
Account background: ScribeHaven is an internal-dev platform used by ~1,500 engineers at a large enterprise software company. Primary goal: replace brittle regexp/grep-based code search with RAG-enabled code-assistant that returns ranked code snippets and contextual docs. Critical constraints: extremely large embedding corpus (~75–120M embeddings over 18 months), frequent re-indexing (nightly + multiple incremental patches per day), and strict SSO/SAML + EU/US data residency needs.

POC summary: initial hosted POC used open code embedding model + L2 index; good MR@1 on small sets but rerank latency explodes when background reindex starts. SE suggested Dedicated pool with shard hot-swap and two-tier index (hot in-memory for last 7 days, cold quantized store for older history). Also proposed use of Redwood Optimize to tune batching & quantization for cost targets.

Metrics / targets shared by customer: target rerank p95 <= 150–200ms for interactive flows, bulk analytical queries can tolerate 1–2s; cost sensitivity: prefer <$0.10 per user-active-query at 2k qps. Indexing: want ability to reindex 20M docs/day with background incremental ingestion and zero-downtime swap.

Security & compliance: must support SSO/SAML with central IdP, SCIM user provisioning, KMS integration for key separation, audit logs retained 1 year, SOC2 attestation required before procurement. Data residency: primary tenants in US with a GDPR-compliant EU region for EU customers.

Quotes / call snippets: "We need a code search that doesn't fall over when our CI pipeline pushes 10k commits overnight." — Eng manager. "If rerank latency creeps above 200ms, dev adoption will stall." — Head of Developer Platform.

Current posture: evaluation-stage POC with plan to pilot Dedicated for 3 months if PRs pass. Main ask from security: SAML metadata + SOC2 docs; from eng: clear performance baseline under frequent reindex cadence.

Next steps (detail): run three Dedicated sizing experiments (small/medium/large) with identical reindex cadence, produce detailed cost-per-query model (tokens + embedding + inference), deliver security package (SOC2 + KMS integration notes), and schedule procurement review for 2026-04.
